name: Retroperitoneal Arteriovenous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Retroperitoneal AVM

criteria.description: Demonstration of abnormal arteriovenous shunting within the retroperitoneal space on angiography or cross-sectional imaging
Presence of pulsatile abdominal mass or bruit in the retroperitoneal region
Exclusion of other vascular malformations or tumors by imaging and clinical evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed arteriovenous shunting in the retroperitoneum plus clinical signs such as pulsatile mass or bruit, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities such as CT angiography, MRI, and catheter angiography.

pathognomonic.notes: Palpable mass with pulsation in the retroperitoneal area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Audible abdominal bruit over retroperitoneal region

common.notes: Due to mass effect or vascular congestion
Localized pain related to vascular engorgement
Vibration felt over the AVM site

occasional.notes: Due to involvement or compression of renal vasculature

searchTerms: symptoms of heart failure with high blood flow
heart failure signs from increased cardiac output
rapid heartbeat and fatigue due to heart strain

occasional.notes: Due to mass effect on adjacent organs

rare.notes: May cause acute pain or infarction
Due to renal artery involvement or compression

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits from spinal cord ischemia
rare.notes: If AVM involves spinal arterial supply
searchTerms: nerve problems from spinal blood loss

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers if thrombosis or ischemia present
imaging: CT angiography showing early venous filling and abnormal vascular nidus
MRI demonstrating flow voids consistent with AVM
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; typically sporadic
other: Physical exam findings of pulsatile mass, bruit, and thrill

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of arteriovenous shunting on imaging
Localization to renal vasculature rather than retroperitoneal space
May present with lower limb ischemia or venous hypertension

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal or flank pain indicating possible rupture or thrombosis
references: Lee BB, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of arteriovenous malformations. J Vasc Surg. 2015.
Yakes WF, et al. Arteriovenous malformations: classification and treatment. Semin Intervent Radiol. 2003.
